source_refs.note: Topic 7.3.1, printed page 150 (Figure 7.5, boxes of particles, carried by the text).

blocks.text: According to the law of mass action, the greater the concentration of the reactants, the more rapidly the reaction proceeds. When the concentration of one or more reactants increases the rate increases, because a higher concentration results in more collisions between the reacting particles, which speeds up the reaction. A box with more reactant particles reacts faster than one with fewer.

blocks.alt: Two square boxes of red and blue particles. Box a) is crowded, with many particles and five orange starbursts where a red and a blue particle collide. Box b) has far fewer particles and only two collisions.
blocks.caption: Figure 7.5: The reaction in box a) will occur faster than that in b) due to the higher concentration (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 7.5).

blocks.title: Did you know
blocks.text: For reactions involving gaseous reactants an increase in pressure increases the concentration of the gases and so the rate of reaction. A pressure change has no effect on the rate if the reactants are solids or liquids.
